items.title: Compactness and normalized invariant form for SU(2)
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Assume the axiom of countable choice. Let
$G=SU(2)=\{U\in M_2(\mathbb C):U^*U=I_2,\ \det U=1\}$ with its real Lie-group
structure. Define the Pauli matrices
$\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$,
$\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and
$\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$, and put
$T_a=-\frac{i}{2}\sigma_a$ for $a\in\{1,2,3\}$. Then $G$ is compact and
noncommutative, its real Lie algebra has basis $T_1,T_2,T_3$ with
$[T_a,T_b]=\sum_{c=1}^3\epsilon_{abc}T_c$, and the real bilinear form
$\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ is positive
definite, symmetric, and invariant under
$\operatorname{Ad}_gX=gXg^{-1}$, with $\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$.

items.title: Classical pure SU(2) Yang–Mills model
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Each instance of the adopted classical pure Yang–Mills model has spacetime $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$,
coordinates $x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3$ of length, orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$, time orientation of increasing
$x^0$, and Lorentz metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use
$c=\hbar=1$, so $x^0=t$, the coordinate and spacetime lengths have unit
$\mathrm m$, and the natural action $S/\hbar$ is dimensionless.

Fix the global structure group $G=SU(2)$, not its quotient $SO(3)$. Each
instance selects a smooth right principal $SU(2)$-bundle $\pi:P\to M$ and
admits only its bundle sector $\Sigma=\{[P]\}$. The matter-representation label set
is empty, so there are no matter fields or current source. The Lie algebra is
$\mathfrak{su}(2)$ with basis $T_a=-i\sigma_a/2$ and positive
$\operatorname{Ad}$-invariant form
$\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, normalized by
$\kappa(T_a,T_b)=\delta_{ab}$. The positive coupling $g_{\mathrm{YM}}$ is a
fixed dimensionless model parameter.

A smooth right principal bundle here has a free and transitive smooth right
$SU(2)$ action on each fibre and equivariant local trivializations; a global
section is not part of the datum. The sector $[P]$ is the class of bundles
smoothly isomorphic to $P$ by equivariant diffeomorphisms over
$\operatorname{id}_M$. The gauge group $\mathcal G(P)$ consists of smooth
diffeomorphisms $\Phi:P\to P$ with $\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and
$\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$. A gauge function $U_i\to SU(2)$ is only a local
description unless a global trivialization has been specified.

A principal connection is a smooth right-invariant horizontal complement
$TP=VP\oplus H$. A gauge field is its connection form $\omega$ with
$\omega(Z_P)=Z$ and $R_g^*\omega=\operatorname{Ad}_{g^{-1}}\omega$, where
$R_g(p)=pg$ and
$Z_P(p)=\left.\frac{d}{dt}\right|_{t=0}p\exp_{SU(2)}(tZ)$. In a local
section $s_i:U_i\to P$, let $A_i=s_i^*\omega$ and let
$F_i=dA_i+\frac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$ be its curvature. Here the bracket is the
alternating-form extension of the Lie bracket, and the local forms on
overlaps satisfy the right-action transition convention
$A_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}A_i+g_{ij}^{-1}dg_{ij}$ and
$F_j=\operatorname{Ad}_{g_{ij}^{-1}}F_i$ when $s_j=s_i g_{ij}$. Thus
$F_i$ represents one global $\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued two-form in the
associated adjoint bundle; the invariant form $\kappa$ makes
$\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i)$ a global scalar four-form.

Adopt the local Lorentzian action density

$$
\mathcal L_{\mathrm{YM}}(A_i)\,d^4x=-\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\,\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i),\qquad [A_i]=\mathrm m^{-1},\quad [F_i]=\mathrm m^{-2}.
$$

For any relatively compact region on which the density is integrable, the
action is its integral. On all of $M$, the action is defined when that
integral converges. Local stationarity is tested through relative action
differences under smooth compactly supported adjoint-bundle-valued
one-form variations; these differences have compact support and are finite.
No boundary values are imposed at infinity. On a finite region, admissible
variations vanish near its boundary. This is an adopted classical model and
normalization, not a theorem, measured law, or claim that a quantum
continuum theory exists.

items.title: Gauge invariance of the classical pure SU(2) Yang–Mills action
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Let $M=\mathbb R^{1,3}$ have orientation
$dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Fix the pure $SU(2)$ model with a
smooth right principal bundle $P\to M$, no matter fields, the form
$\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$ on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$, and fixed
$g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$. For a smooth connection with local curvature $F_i$,
the adopted action density is
$-\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i)/(2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2)$.

For every smooth gauge transformation $\Phi:P\to P$ satisfying
$\pi\circ\Phi=\pi$ and $\Phi(pg)=\Phi(p)g$, let $\Phi_*H=d\Phi(H)$ be its
action on a principal connection $H$. Then the local curvature density is
unchanged in every section, so every defined local action and every
convergent global action are invariant under $H\mapsto\Phi_*H$. More
precisely, for any local section $s_i:U_i\to P$, define the smooth local map
$v_i:U_i\to SU(2)$ by
$\Phi^{-1}\circ s_i=s_i v_i$. The transformed curvature components satisfy
$F_i^{\Phi}=\operatorname{Ad}_{v_i^{-1}}F_i$. Each $v_i$ is local data; the
statement assumes no global map $M\to SU(2)$ for a possibly nontrivial
bundle.

items.title: Source-free Euler–Lagrange equation for the classical SU(2) Yang–Mills action
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Use the adopted pure $SU(2)$ model on oriented, time-oriented Minkowski
$\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, no matter fields,
$\kappa(X,Y)=-2\operatorname{Tr}_2(XY)$, and fixed $g_{\mathrm{YM}}>0$.
For a local section $s_i:U_i\to P$, write
$A_i=s_i^*\omega$,
$F_i=dA_i+\frac12[A_i\wedge A_i]$, and
$D_{A_i}\eta=d\eta+[A_i\wedge\eta]$ for an
$\mathfrak{su}(2)$-valued differential form $\eta$. A smooth local
variation is any $a\in\Omega^1(U_i,\mathfrak{su}(2))$ with compact support
in $U_i$; it represents a global adjoint-bundle-valued connection variation
by extension by zero. Define its dimensionless relative action difference by
$$
\Delta(S/\hbar)_i(\varepsilon;a)=-\frac{1}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\int_{U_i}\left(\kappa(F_{A_i+\varepsilon a}\wedge *_\eta F_{A_i+\varepsilon a})-\kappa(F_i\wedge *_\eta F_i)\right).
$$
The integrand difference is compactly supported, so this relative integral is
defined even if the unvaried action over all of $M$ diverges.

The connection is stationary when the derivative at $\varepsilon=0$ of
$\Delta(S/\hbar)_i(\varepsilon;a)$ vanishes for every such variation in every
local trivialization.
It is stationary if and only if
$D_{A_i}(*_\eta F_i)=0$ in every local section. The local equations transform
by the adjoint action on overlaps and therefore define the global,
source-free Yang–Mills equation on the selected bundle sector. This
equivalence is a conditional classical deduction from the adopted action
and compact-support boundary convention.

items.title: A noncommuting SU(2) configuration with nonzero Yang–Mills density
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Specialize the adopted model to the trivial bundle
$P=\mathbb R^{1,3}\times SU(2)$ with its product section. Let $T_1,T_2,T_3$
be the normalized basis of the model, so $[T_1,T_2]=T_3$ and
$\kappa(T_3,T_3)=1$. For a constant $a\ne0$ with unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$, take
the smooth connection potential
$A=a(T_1\,dx^1+T_2\,dx^2)$. Its curvature is
$F=a^2T_3\,dx^1\wedge dx^2$, and its Lorentzian action density is
$-\frac{a^4}{2g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2}\,
dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$. This is a field configuration;
no stationarity or field-equation claim is made.

items.title: A nonzero pure-gauge potential with zero Yang–Mills density
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Specialize the adopted model to the trivial bundle
$P=\mathbb R^{1,3}\times SU(2)$ with canonical section $s$. Let
$T_3=-i\sigma_3/2$ and choose a length $\ell>0$. Change section to
$s^u(x)=s(x)u(x)$ with
$u(x)=\exp(T_3\sin(x^0/\ell))$. The connection whose potential in $s$ is
$A=0$ has potential in $s^u$
$A^u=u^{-1}du=T_3\ell^{-1}\cos(x^0/\ell)\,dx^0$, which is nonzero. Its
Cartan curvature and Yang–Mills action density are zero. This is a change
of gauge description of a classical connection, not a distinct physical
observation.

items.title: A nonzero null plane-wave solution of the pure SU(2) model
items.design_state: Step 1 authoring and scoped checks complete; readiness is recorded in the native per-item Step 1 record.
items.statement:
Specialize the adopted model to the trivial bundle
$P=\mathbb R^{1,3}\times SU(2)$ with its canonical section. Let
$q=x^0-x^3$, choose a length $\ell>0$ and a nonzero constant $b$ with unit
$\mathrm m^{-1}$, and set
$A=T_3 b\sin(q/\ell)\,dx^1$. Its curvature is
$F=T_3(b/\ell)\cos(q/\ell)(dx^0-dx^3)\wedge dx^1$, which is not identically
zero. With orientation $dx^0\wedge dx^1\wedge dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, this connection satisfies
$D_A(*_\eta F)=0$ and $\kappa(F\wedge *_\eta F)=0$. It is therefore a
stationary source-free solution of the adopted classical model; no
uniqueness, quantum, or empirical claim is made.
